language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hello, I am Tim.

Hi! We’re in Brazil, welcome to Rio! Bem-vindo ao Rio! My name’s Ricardo, but you can call me Rick, and I’m glad to show you one of the greatest and funniest Carnival parades in the world, are you ready to join the party? We’ll have a great time, but we’ll also learn a lot here!
For Carnival, you need a costume, do you like mine? I chose to be... a skeleton! I want to celebrate something special that happens when living organisms die.
Death is irreversible, that means, once something dies it can’t come back to life. But death is not the end! Actually, it is the beginning of a cycle. Let’s join the parade and find out more!
Older organisms die to make space and give new, young individuals a chance to grow, so there is less competition for resources.
Hello, I am Tim.

Hi! We’re in Brazil, welcome to Rio! Bem-vindo ao Rio! My name’s Ricardo, but you can call me Rick, and I’m glad to show you one of the greatest and funniest Carnival parades in the world, are you ready to join the party? We’ll have a great time, but we’ll also learn a lot here!
For Carnival, you need a costume, do you like mine? I chose to be... a skeleton! I want to celebrate something special that happens when living organisms die.
Death is irreversible, that means, once something dies it can’t come back to life. But death is not the end! Actually, it is the beginning of a cycle. Let’s join the parade and find out more!
Older organisms die to make space and give new, young individuals a chance to grow, so there is less competition for resources.

A typical element in the Rio Carnival are the floats. They are often inspired by a theme. Today, the themes are 'scavengers', 'detritus eaters' and 'decomposers'. These are important elements in the after-death cycle. Do you know what they are?
When an organism dies, it decays and rots away – we say that the body decomposes.
Some animals and organisms are involved in this process, we call them scavengers, detritus eaters and decomposers.
A scavenger finds dead bodies of animals and eats the remains.
A detritus eater eats the waste matter produced by other animals.
A decomposer transforms waste and dead matter into good substances which are then absorbed by the soil, from which plants can grow.

The death of living organisms plays an important role in the carbon cycle, do you know what that is? Carbon is a natural element which can be found in living and non-living things like rocks, air, water, plants and animals. All life is build from carbon! With "carbon cycle" we mean the circulation of carbon back and forth between living things and the environment. The cycle works like this:

Plants absorb carbon from the air and ground. Animals take in carbon from plants when they eat. As plants and animals die, decomposers eat them and turn the matter into minerals and gases. This is how carbon returns to the ground and air.
Here you see a description of one of the phases from the carbon cycle, can you find the picture that matches it?
